memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said, 'There is a place near me where you may stand on a rock. When my glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft in the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.'" - Exod 33:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God says no to the request, and then makes a way. "There is a place near me."

Look at the tenderness in the arrangement. A rock to stand on. A cleft to be hidden in. God's own hand covering Moses while the glory passes. Every detail is God protecting a man from what would otherwise destroy him — so that he can experience as much of God as a human being can safely bear.

This is how God deals with us. He does not hand us more than we can survive. He shelters us in order to reveal Himself to us.

Christians have long seen a picture of Christ here, and rightly so — not by inventing symbolism, but because Scripture itself teaches that our safety before God is found in being hidden in Another. "Your life is now hidden with Christ in God" (Col 3:3). We stand before holy glory not on our own record but sheltered by Him.

And notice: the shelter is not away from God. It is "near me." God's protection does not push us to a safe distance; it draws us close.

Wherever you are today, there is a place near Him for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you seen God shelter you from what you could not have handled?
2. What does it mean that your life is hidden with Christ in God?
3. Are you seeking a place near God, or keeping a safe distance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for making a place near You where I can stand. Keep me hidden in Christ. Amen.
